questions.question_text: Under WV law, which activity requires a real estate license when performed for compensation?
questions.correct_answer: Negotiating the sale of real estate
distractors: Painting a house for a homeowner
Mowing a rental property's lawn
Installing a fence on private property
questions.explanation: Negotiating the sale, exchange, purchase, or rental of real estate for compensation requires a license. Physical property maintenance does not require a license.

questions.question_text: An unlicensed person collects rent on several apartment buildings owned by different, unrelated owners, charging each owner a monthly fee. Does this require a WV real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, collecting rent for compensation requires a license
distractors: No, rent collection never requires a license
Only if the building has 10+ units
Only if the person also manages repairs
questions.explanation: Collecting rent for compensation falls within the §30-40-4 definition of a broker, and "property management" is itself a defined licensed activity. Watch the boundary: §30-40-5(c)(8) exempts a person "employed exclusively to act as the management or rental agent for the real estate of one person or entity," and (c)(2) exempts an owner's regular employees who perform incidental acts without extra compensation. Serving several unrelated owners for a fee falls outside both exemptions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following activities does NOT require a WV real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: Selling your own property as the owner
distractors: Listing property for sale for a fee
Procuring prospects for a commission
Advertising real estate services for pay
questions.explanation: The exemption covers "any person acting on his or her own behalf as owner or lessor of real estate" (§30-40-5(c)(1)). The Commission's rule goes further for licensees: under 174-1-17.5, "a licensee who is the owner of the property has all the rights of an unlicensed person with regard to that property." Listing, procuring prospects and advertising real estate services for compensation all require a license.

questions.question_text: A person advertises themselves as a real estate professional and helps buyers find properties for a fee. Do they need a WV license?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, advertising as a real estate professional requires a license
distractors: No, only selling property requires a license
Only if they also negotiate purchase offers
Only if they handle commercial properties
questions.explanation: Advertising or holding oneself out as being engaged in the real estate business, and assisting or directing in the procuring of prospects, are both licensed activities.

questions.question_text: An unlicensed auctioneer is hired by a private seller to auction a farm. Does this require a WV real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, auctioning real estate requires a license
distractors: No, auctioneers have a separate license
Only for commercial properties
Only if the auction exceeds $100,000
questions.explanation: Auctioning real estate for compensation is within the §30-40-4 definition of a broker, so a real estate license is required here. The exemption is narrow: §30-40-5(c)(9) excuses a person licensed as an auctioneer under §19-2C-1 et seq. only when retained by a receiver or trustee in bankruptcy, a fiduciary acting under a deed of trust or will, or a fiduciary of a decedent's estate. A private seller is none of those.

questions.question_text: An attorney helps a client buy property as part of their legal services. Does the attorney need a WV real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: No, attorneys acting in professional capacity are exempt
distractors: Yes, all real estate transactions require a license
Only if the attorney receives a commission
Only if the property exceeds $250,000
questions.explanation: Attorneys-at-law are exempt (§30-40-5(c)(3)). Note the proviso: an attorney who wants a broker's license must still pass the written examination required by §30-40-12, unless licensed as a broker before July 1, 1980. An attorney applicant may also submit a State Bar letter of good standing in lieu of the criminal history check (§30-40-11(f)).

questions.question_text: A court appoints a trustee to sell a deceased person's real estate. Does the trustee need a WV license?
questions.correct_answer: No, persons acting under court order are exempt
distractors: Yes, selling real estate always requires a license
Only if the property is worth over $50,000
Only if the trustee receives compensation
questions.explanation: Persons acting under court order — including executors, administrators, trustees, and guardians — are exempt from licensure requirements.

questions.question_text: A public officer negotiates the acquisition of land for a highway project as part of their official duties. Do they need a WV real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: No, a public officer performing official duties is exempt
distractors: Yes, the state has no special exemption
Only if the land value exceeds $500,000
Only if they negotiate the purchase price
questions.explanation: The exemption covers "a public officer while performing his or her official duties" (§30-40-5(c)(6)). Read it narrowly — the exemption is written for public officers, not for every government employee. A separate exemption, §30-40-5(c)(7), covers anyone acquiring or disposing of properties for easements and rights of way.

questions.question_text: Which of the following persons is NOT exempt from WV real estate licensure?
questions.correct_answer: A friend who helps sell a home for a fee
distractors: An owner selling their own property
An executor selling estate property
A government employee acquiring land
questions.explanation: Anyone who sells another person's real estate for compensation must be licensed. The exemptions in §30-40-5(c) cover owners acting for themselves, executors and others acting under a court order or will, and public officers on official duty — a friend paid to help sell a home fits none of them.

questions.question_text: The key factor that triggers the WV real estate license requirement is performing activities for what?
distractors: Any real estate-related activity
Activities involving property over $10,000
Only activities involving residential property
questions.explanation: Every branch of the §30-40-4 "broker" definition begins "for compensation or with the intention or expectation of receiving or collecting compensation." §30-40-23 sharpens the point: a single act performed for compensation, or with the expectation or promise of compensation, is enough to make a person a broker, associate broker or salesperson subject to the article.
